page: Microsoft Azure E4d_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the server provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores using hyper-threading. The system configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. Cache resources consist of 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 35 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512_VNNI, and AES. It also bundles 161 GB of local SSD temporary storage, contains zero GPUs, and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark assessments demonstrate moderate single-threaded responsiveness coupled with constrained multi-core and uncached throughput. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1234.0 and gzip compression throughput of 23.84 GB/sec. Conversely, compute-intensive multi-threaded tasks sit in the lower quartile, reflected by a Geekbench multi-core score of 2747.0 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 3707.88. Uncached memory operations yield 22.87 GB/sec for read bandwidth and 17.84 GB/sec for write bandwidth on large 256 MB blocks, while PassMark database operations register at 1382.57 and Redis SET throughput reaches 3.55 million operations per second.

The primary efficiency tradeoff of the E4d_v4 lies in its high memory density and integrated local SSD capacity relative to a lower overall CPU throughput ceiling. Workloads with substantial RAM requirements do not need to overprovision unnecessary compute cores to satisfy memory footprint demands. The instance is suited for mid-sized relational database management systems, in-memory caches, operational staging environments, and batch extract, transform, load jobs that rely on substantial RAM buffers and fast scratch disk space rather than extensive multi-core compute scaling.
